source.title: NetFlowGen: Leveraging Generative Pre-training for Network Traffic Dynamics
source.authors: Jiawei Zhou; Woojeong Kim; Zhiying Xu; Alexander M. Rush; Minlan Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study applies generative pre-training to network traffic and reports validation loss at several model sizes. This is a new modality relative to language-model scaling, but it does not fit or test a power-law curve.
record.gate_note: The study also reports next-step prediction against a statistical baseline and downstream DDoS-detection results. Those are not results on loss scaling or the power-law shape, so they are not rows here. Table 10 reports validation accuracy, perplexity and F1 as well as loss; only loss bears on V5.
record.test_reason: The study pre-trains Transformer decoders on network traffic, a new modality, and reports best validation loss at 1.9M–25M parameters (Table 10). That is a direct, though small and unfitted, result on whether loss falls with parameters outside text. It fits no power law, and data may be the bottleneck.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find pre-training loss agnostic to the sizes tested and use the smallest (1.9M) model for efficiency. They say the loss patterns resemble the NLP observation that bigger models are more data-efficient (citing Kaplan). They leave the size–data relationship and larger-scale scaling to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Generative next-step prediction on multivariate NetFlow traffic with a Transformer decoder; the reported size sweep is not the original language-model scaling-law fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The sweep varies parameter count and, for some configurations, learning rate and dropout; reported validation loss varies across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing learning rate or dropout at a fixed size moves validation loss by up to 0.004. That is comparable to the whole 1.9M→25M size effect (0.005).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small-scale traffic pre-training, hyperparameter choices matter as much as model size for validation loss.

record.problems: The model-size range is limited; the study does not fit power laws, report uncertainty for Table 10, or test larger-scale extrapolation. The Table 10 layout does not unambiguously associate one parameter count with a configuration.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponent; no data or compute scaling; only about 1.1 orders of magnitude in parameters. Image and video models, repeated data, and fine-tuning/transfer scaling are not examined.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
Size and shape are varied together; there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Downstream DDoS results use only the 1.9M model; there is no relation to scale or loss.
No fitting choices or comparison of published laws.

record.verdict_notes: Table 10 is flattened. Merged LR cells give five LR values over seven rows: 1.9M×2, 5.4M at LR 0.0001 ×1, 5.4M at LR 0.0005 ×2, 12M, 25M. The record's '7.2M' model is a section-heading artifact. The only clean size comparison is at LR 0.0005 with dropout 0.3. This is a weak test: tiny models, about one order of magnitude in parameters, a single run per setting, and no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study is about network traffic, not language-model held-out pretraining loss.
It does not fit on small runs and evaluate predictions on much larger runs.
It does not compare parameter/token allocations at fixed compute.
It does not compare architecture details at a fixed parameter count for this claim.
Only network-traffic generative pre-training is examined. Image and video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested; the study does not fit a power law or test its shape.
Downstream detection is evaluated, but the study does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
The study varies some model and training settings but does not examine disagreement between published scaling laws, fitting choices for power laws, or departures from a fitted curve.

rows.subject: NetFlowGen Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss across Transformer sizes and training settings.
rows.note: A separate learning-rate and dropout setting for the stated model configuration.
rows.check: 5.4M at LR 0.0005 with dropout 0.1, a dropout variant. Reading Table 10's merged cells, the order is 0.3,0.1,0.3,0.1,0.3,0.3,0.3. On that reading this row may actually be dropout 0.1 (0.182) or swapped with R5. It is a hyperparameter variant, not on the matched size axis.

rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss across Transformer sizes.
rows.note: Table layout does not unambiguously associate this parameter count with a model configuration.
rows.check: Wrong subject size. '7.2' is the misplaced section heading '7.2 Traffic Feature Diversity', not a parameter count. Table 10 has no 7.2M model, so this row is the third 4-4-256-1024 (5.4M) entry at LR 0.0005, dropout 0.3 (loss 0.183). That is a small drop from 0.186 at 1.9M.

rows.subject: NetFlowGen Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss across Transformer sizes.
rows.note: The text says the tested models are agnostic to size, while noting that loss patterns are similar to an observation in NLP; no power-law fit is given.
rows.check: 12M at the matched setting (LR 0.0005, dropout 0.3): 0.181 vs 0.186 at 1.9M. This is about a 3% drop over 6x parameters; the authors call performance agnostic to size.

rows.subject: NetFlowGen Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation loss across Transformer sizes.
rows.note: The validation loss is slightly higher than the reported 12M-parameter result; the study does not assess whether this departs from a fitted curve.
rows.check: 25M at the matched setting: 0.182, no improvement over 12M (0.181). Loss plateaus rather than continuing to fall.

relationships.condition: Network-traffic (NetFlow) generative pre-training, 1.9M–25M parameters, fixed data (~97k training series), LR 0.0005, dropout 0.3
relationships.reason: Loss falls only 0.186→0.183→0.181, then 0.182 at 25M (R1, R5, R6, R7). The authors call the models agnostic to size. The data bottleneck is not ruled out and no power law is fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased from 0.186 to 0.183 to 0.181 before rising to 0.182 at 25M parameters, without a fitted power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
